A semi-literal English rendering of the Latin text, created for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model made by Anthropic. It is a crib to help the reader with the Latin, and should not be treated as a separate translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: Iud Dei XII 21.5
div.ab: neque nocens quęrentibus ueritatem impune possit illudere te, quem occulta non transeunt, ostendente et uirtute tua, qui secretorum es cognitor, declarante.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 422 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: nor the guilty be able with impunity to mock those who seek the truth, you, whom hidden things do not pass by, showing [it], and your power, who are the knower of secrets, declaring [it].
